A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete text, equations and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison, including the table added in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports mathematical bounds and proofs, including in its appendices, but no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical. Its added discussion of experiments on heavy-tailed data and hyperparameter robustness explicitly attributes those results to Birrell et al. (2022b).

M1.justification: The (f, Γ)-GAN objectives and empirical optimization formulation in Equations (3)–(7) are retained. The added divergence examples do not introduce an algorithmic component or change the procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts dataset-based training or evaluation. Expanded references to heavy-tailed distributions and mutual-information estimation concern theoretical applicability or cited work.

E2.justification: Neither version reports an experimentally evaluated comparator set. The new comparison with Arora et al. (2017) in Section 1.2 concerns prior theory.

E3.justification: No experimental protocols are introduced or revised. The new discussion of choosing generator-noise sample size m much larger than data sample size n interprets existing bounds rather than reporting a changed evaluation setting.

E4.justification: Neither version reports original ablations, robustness experiments or case studies. The added hyperparameter-robustness discussion summarizes experiments attributed to earlier work.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The theoretical concentration inequalities are retained.

E6.justification: No original empirical result entries are added or revised. The analytical bounds, including the constants and O(sqrt(k/n)) rate in Equations (52)–(53), remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, bounds and proofs are retained, including Theorem 3.12 renumbered as 3.13 and Appendices A–F. Table 1 supplies standard formulas for previously named divergences; moving the declaration of α and β within Assumption 3.2 does not change its requirements.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion newly emphasize independent applications of the Rademacher bounds beyond GANs. The introduction also qualifies its research-gap claim by acknowledging existing nonlinear-GAN guarantees from Arora et al. (2017), while retaining the central consistency claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 newly explains why m much larger than n can make the statistical error terms nearly match the IPM case, and why reversing the divergence arguments changes this conclusion. Section 1.1 explains the discriminator approximation tradeoff. Appendix E removes its earlier statement excluding consideration of heavy-tailed distributions, without changing its theorem.

D1.justification: The implementation guidance about absorbing the shift into the final-layer bias and using Equation (6) is unchanged. No training configurations, hardware details or code/data access information are added.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands its positioning relative to nonlinear-GAN theory. New Section 1.2 identifies Arora et al. (2017) as the closest prior work and distinguishes objective structure, guarantee meaning and support assumptions. Additional references cover other nonlinear-GAN frameworks and mutual-information estimation.

P1.justification: The introduction gains a dedicated comparison subsection and expanded motivation. Local explanatory paragraphs, terminology and citation formatting are revised elsewhere, while the main section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 1 displaying f, its convex conjugate and z0 for JS, KL and α-divergences. The existing single-column layout is retained, with text and equations reflowing around the additions.

improvement.justification: Section 1.2 addresses v2's omission of closely related nonlinear-GAN theory and better qualifies the contribution. Table 1 and the added sampling-regime discussion make the retained results easier to understand and apply. These support a limited overall improvement while the mathematical guarantees and proofs remain unchanged.
